newsitem.title: USA: Florida customs officer nabbed for cocaine smuggling.
newsitem.headline: Florida customs officer nabbed for cocaine smuggling.

text.p: Narcotics agents have arrested a U.S. customs inspector alleged to have used her position to smuggle cocaine through Fort Lauderdale airport, the U.S. Attorney's Office in Miami said on Thursday.

Laurel Anderson, 46, her husband William, 48, and son Keir, 24, were arrested on Wednesday and charged with conspiracy to import and possess cocaine and with bribery, William Keefer, U.S. Attorney for south Florida, said in a statement.

The indictment said that from September to December this year, the Andersons conspired to import more than 220 pounds (100 kg) of cocaine from the Bahamas though Fort Lauderdale airport concealed in luggage and in cars.

Laurel Anderson, a customs officer since 1988, is also charged with receiving a $7,500 bribe from an undercover Drug Enforcement Agency (DEA) agent in connecton with the conspiracy. Her husanbd is also charged with aiding and abetting receipt of the bribe.
If convicted, they face maximum sentences of life imprisonment and fines of up to $4 million.
